recentItems.title: Morocco elections: Ceuta, Israel and football shape results despite low turnout
recentItems.description:
Morocco’s parliamentary elections were about much more than just politics.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

The Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM), emerged as the largest party with 97 seats, up from 87 in the 2021 election, overtaking the National Rally of Independents (RNI) that led the last government.

They were bolstered by the recruitment of Fouzi Lekjaa, leader of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation, weeks before the vote, who was widely seen as the driving force behind the competitive transformation of Morocco’s national football team.

But behind the football hype is deep frustration among many young Moroccans, some of which came to a head when more than 70,000 people crossed from Morocco towards the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, in one of the biggest migration surges in its history.

recentItems.title: Could ERITREA and ETHIOPIA end up in full scale WAR?
recentItems.description:
Hundreds of thousands of people were killed in a two-year between Tigrayan forces and Ethiopia's government which ended in a peace deal in 2022. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Today the trauma and fear of war creeps back in as both sides accuse each other of launching new offensives. 

Earlier this week the TPLF announced a new coalition alongside other militias - some of whom had previously been bitter opponents.

The so-called Alliance for survival is made up of seven armed rebel groups which have been waging their own battles against the Ethiopian government in different parts of the country.

Tigrayan forces have seized three airports in Tigray, and in response Ethiopian airlines have suspended all flights to the region. 

But why are things escalating now? Is the clock ticking for the Ethiopian government? And will Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed achieve his goal of accessing the Red Sea? 

To understand things better and break it all down we’re joined by Tsedale Lemma, an Ethiopian journalist and founder of the Addis Standard and Nicholas Westcott, former director of the Royal African Society.

recentItems.title: Alexei Sayle on Gaza, Marxism and why people “should stop believing lies”
recentItems.description:
Alexei Sayle has spent a lifetime mixing comedy with politics, protest and an instinctive suspicion of authority.

Raised in a communist household in Liverpool, he became one of the defining figures of alternative comedy before building a career as a writer, actor and political activist. His latest book, How I’ve Tried to Change the World by Walking Down the Middle of the Street Shouting, looks back at decades of marches, political battles, defeats and moments of hope.

In this episode of Ways to Change the World, Alexei talks to Krishnan Guru-Murthy about Gaza and Israel, and his feelings on the “genocide” of Palestinians (which Israel denies), his Jewish identity, whether protest actually works, why he remains a Marxist, growing up surrounded by communism and how politics shaped his comedy.

He also reflects on falling out of fashion in the 1990s, his unlikely success on TikTok, why comedy should never become a political lecture and why, after decades of campaigning, he still hasn’t entirely given up on changing the world.
